original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: An opt-in publication preflight uses bounded joint reachability while preserving the original byte/mode check, source-history acceptance, ordinary diagnostics and source isolation.
scope_change_reason: The publication script is a frozen live input elsewhere, so the same measured optimization is delivered as an opt-in adapter. Existing shared scripts and tests remain byte-identical to the base.
bottleneck_link: This verifier-engineering result reduces the latency of source-bound publication checks; it does not change either supplier or kappa.
stop_rule: Ship the first complete-preflight gain with equal receipts and passing rejection controls; do not expand the algorithm after that.
evidence: BENCHMARK.json contains seven alternating fresh-process pairs, complete equal receipts, implementation hashes and separate diagnostic profiles. The registered checks run all 18 source-history tests.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: How does the joint walk behave on much larger histories with 32 to 256 distinct ancestor pins?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Shared traversal can have different costs from separate commit-graph queries; no universal speedup is established.
open_questions.first_step: Use a real publication with those pins and alternate complete CLI runs, retaining identical receipts and independent rejection controls.
open_questions.blocked_by: A representative large-pin publication fixture and a separate measurement budget.
